inputCoverage.osmSnapshot: 2026-08-11 Protomaps z14; 6×6 tile window before our conflation
inputCoverage.agencyScope: Complete features intersecting input window from existing source cache; not a fresh agency census

recommendation.summary: The two representations are nearly coincident. Keep one geometry and transfer useful attributes; there is little evidence for drawing both.
reasons: OpenStreetMap: 100% of its geometry lies within 15 m of the other source; 100% within 50 m. Median nearest-line offset 0.6 m.
NPS: 99% of its geometry lies within 15 m of the other source; 100% within 50 m. Median nearest-line offset 0.5 m.

Within the same input window, OpenStreetMap: 572 m long, median vertex spacing 9.1 m, 0 m outside the other source’s 50 m corridor; NPS: 591 m long, median vertex spacing 11.7 m, 0 m outside the other source’s 50 m corridor.

Endpoint check: OpenStreetMap has 0 non-seam endpoint candidates over 75 m from the other alignment; NPS has 0 non-seam endpoint candidates over 75 m from the other alignment. These can be real additions, branches, or source gaps; inspect their connections.
Vertex density measures representation detail, not survey accuracy. Sharp turns may be genuine switchbacks; geometry alone cannot diagnose GPS multipath.
recommendation.limitations: Heuristic guidance, not an independent ground-truth verdict. Uses source geometry and frozen DEM only; no imagery interpretation or route editing. DEM measures ground surface, not surveyed trail elevation. Full agency inputs and OSM tile fragments have different lineage; no automatic edits.
